gloss: just a moment ago; just now

definitions.gloss: just a moment ago; only a short while ago
definitions.explanation: つい (just, only) intensifying さっき (a while ago): stresses that very little time has passed, typically minutes rather than hours. Casual, spoken register.

examples.japanese: ついさっき{帰|かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: I got back just a moment ago.

examples.japanese: ついさっきまで{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていた。
examples.english: It was raining until just a moment ago.

examples.japanese: ついさっき{電話|でんわ}があったばかりなのに、もう{用件|ようけん}を{忘|わす}れてしまった。
examples.english: He called only a moment ago, and I've already forgotten what it was about.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- ついさっきまで: until just a moment ago
- ついさっき〜たばかり: to have only just done something
- ついさっきのこと: something that happened just now

SIMILAR WORDS:
- さっき: a while ago — the plain form, vaguer and possibly an hour or more back
- たった{今|いま}: this very moment — even more immediate, and usable in writing
- {先|さき}ほど: a short while ago — the polite equivalent, used in business speech

REGISTER:
Conversational. In polite or written contexts, use {先|さき}ほど instead.
